mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.25% compresses risk-free rates, reducing discount factors for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 20-day returns as market participants adjust to lower opportunity costs.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points (mo/mo) signals accelerating inflation that erodes real corporate margins and triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp (mo/mo) (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2% annualized and CPIAUCSL exceeding 3% year-over-year signals overheating that forces central banks to tighten, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to valuation compression.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods meeting the trigger condition (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 6.0%), a monthly PAYEMS decline exceeding 0.1% signals labor market deterioration that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, generating negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 6.0% and PAYEMS declines (mo/mo) (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Residential housing starts (HOUST) above 650 thousand units signals robust consumer demand for housing, which correlates with positive equity market sentiment and drives positive S&P 500 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST > 650 (thousands) (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous INDPRO decline below 95.0 and HOUST decline below 650 thousand units signals manufacturing contraction and housing demand weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 60-day returns due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods meeting the trigger condition (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly FEDFUNDS increase exceeding 0.25 percentage points (mo/mo) signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity liquidity and valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp (mo/mo) (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 3.0% annualized), RSAFS decline below 400,000 million dollars signals reduced consumer credit strength that triggers negative S&P 500 60-day returns due to slowing consumption.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 > 3.0% and RSAFS declines (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
